ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Information for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (Act No. 18968, effective Mar. 23, 2021), as amended, Articles 5-2 and 5-3; Enforcement Decree of the Specific Financial Information Act (Presidential Decree No. 30925, effective Jul. 1, 2020), as amended; Financial Transaction Reports Act (Act No. 18795, effective Feb. 3, 2021), as amended; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 18542, effective Jan. 1, 2022), as amended; Commercial Act (Act No. 17928, effective Feb. 14, 2021), as amended, Articles 18-24 and 543-555.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder (Certificate of Corporate Registration or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registrar in the country of origin (e.g., Registrar of Companies, Companies House, or court registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative: (A) Hague Apostille route for Apostille Convention states: notarize in origin, obtain Apostille from the origin state's designated competent authority, attach certified Korean translation; (B) Consular Legalization route for non-Apostille states: notarize in origin, legalize through the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in the origin state. The two routes are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of No Change / ex officio record) for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin-country company registry or competent tax authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative: (A) notarize plus Apostille under the Hague Convention if the origin state is a member; (B) notarize, origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then Korean consular legalization if the origin state is not an Apostille member. Never use both routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the Korean incorporation filing and identifying the local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate shareholder, notarized before a licensed notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative: (A) Apostille route: notarize then apostillize through the competent authority of the origin state; (B) Consular route: notarize, authenticate through origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Republic of Korea consulate. Do not chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Constitutional Documents / Memorandum and Articles) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or custodian of records of the shareholder in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative: (A) Apostille if origin is a Hague member; (B) origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization plus Korean consular legalization if origin is not a Hague member. These are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each material source of incorporation funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed bank or financial institution in the country of origin where the shareholder maintains a relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative: (A) bank letter notarized and apostillized if the origin state is an Apostille member; (B) bank letter notarized, legalized by origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then by the Korean Embassy/Consulate for non-Apostille states. Never combine both methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports / national identity documents for each director, ultimate beneficial owner, and authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or licensed notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel alternative: notarized copies followed by either Hague Apostille or Korean consular legalization depending on the origin state's membership in the Apostille Convention. The two paths are mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to acceptance of any engagement or subscription, the lead AML/CFT officer must screen all directors, members, UBOs, signatories, representatives, material counterparties, and beneficial trust arrangements against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN and SSI lists, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) restricted and sanction lists, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Korean domestic sanctions list issued by the Ministry of Economy and Finance. Each screening must include exact identifier matching, alias/transliteration matching, nationality, passport, tax residence, and adverse-media review. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to politically exposed persons (PEPs), relatives/close associates of PEPs, legal persons with nominee shareholders or bearer-share history, and all non-resident investors. Negative screening results must be evidenced in the CDD file, refreshed at least every 90 days during onboarding, and retained for a minimum of five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea and the district court commercial registration divisions; post-filing business name registration is completed through the Hometax Business Registration Portal of the National Tax Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Commercial Act Article 18, the registered trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be written in Hangul. Any foreign-language brand or English corporate name may be used only as a secondary identifier and must be transliterated into Hangul in the articles of incorporation and in the commercial registration. The required four-tier naming convention is: (1) a distinctive brand or geographic prefix; (2) an actual business-purpose descriptor corresponding to the filed ISIC/NAICS scope, such as specialty tea salon, tea lounge, teacup salon, or loose-leaf tea service; (3) the statutory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (4) an optional sequential or unique designator if the first three tiers are identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The registry will reject a name that is misleading about the nature, qualification, or quality of the business, or that uses prohibited terms without ministerial approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A trade name reservation made through IROS is valid for 180 days and cannot be extended. If the incorporation registration is not completed within 180 days, the reservation lapses and a new search and reservation must be filed. If the registry judge rejects a name or incorporation registration as identical or misleading, the applicant may file a written objection, known as an immediate appeal, with the competent district court within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice. The appeal must attach the rejection notice, the objection on grounds of priority or non-confusion, a comparative list of registered names, and the date-time stamp of the original name search. If the court dismisses the appeal, the applicant may immediately file an amended name application without prejudice, preserving the original incorporation documentation where possible.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, co-working address, or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered principal place of business for a Yuhan Hoesa operating a specialty tea salon and cultural ceramic lounge. Korean commercial registration and municipal food-service licensing require a fixed physical address with an actual storefront, beverage-preparation area, seating, restroom, sanitation facilities, and the capacity to satisfy the Food Sanitation Act (general restaurant / tea shop category). The National Tax Service, district registry court, municipal licensing office, and acquiring banks will separately require physical confirmation of the operating premises before issuing a business registration certificate, food-service license, and credit-card/POS merchant agreement. A virtual office may be used solely as an auxiliary management or communications address; using it as the registered seat would cause rejection of the business license, suspension of the credit-card terminal, and tax-residence recharacterization.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical-inspection checklist: (1) registered address must equal the lease and the operational storefront; (2) visible Korean-language exterior signage matching the registered name

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 543 through 568 governing the formation, governance, officers, and registration of a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company, together with the Corporate Tax Act and Value-Added Tax Act for mandatory business registration and tax identification obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of Yuhan Hoesa, accessible through the Supreme Court of Korea eCourt portal (www.scourt.go.kr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration of a Yuhan Hoesa (법인설립등기신청서) filed with authenticated Articles of Incorporation, paid-in capital certificate, and statutory officer appointment documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa. The capital amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully subscribed and deposited into a corporate bank account before the registration filing, and such funds must remain available until the company registration certificate is issued. There is no mandatory escrow blocked account requirement, except for practical safeguards imposed by the receiving bank. Non-resident ownership is permitted up to 100 percent for this specialty tea salon business class.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION
YUHANG HOESA (Republic of Korea Limited Company)
Corporate Registration No. [●]

RESOLVED, by the incorporated shareholders in general meeting assembled, and by the first board of directors of Yuhan Hoesa, acting in writing in lieu of a formal board meeting, effective immediately, as follows:

1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The subscribers have subscribed to and agreed to take the shares or contribution rights in Yuhan Hoesa in the amounts set forth in the share subscription schedule. The board of directors confirms the aggregate initial paid-in capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation and instructs the Representative Director to deposit the proceeds into the corporate bank account and to obtain the Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit required for registration.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company shall be situated at [full street address], Republic of Korea, and the board adopts that location as the legal seat and address for service of process, notices, and governmental correspondence. The board directs the Representative Director and Corporate Secretary to execute the lease agreement, obtain the owner written consent, and file the registered office details with the competent Company Registration Court.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The board authorizes the opening of checking, savings, and foreign currency accounts with [authorized commercial bank], and resolves that banking transactions shall require two authorized signatures, namely the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer, provided that transactions below KRW [●] may be executed by the Representative Director alone. The bank account opening forms and signatory cards are approved.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The following persons are appointed as statutory officers of the Company: [Name], Representative Director; [Name], Director and Chief Financial Officer; and [Name], Auditor, if required under the Commercial Act. Each appointee is confirmed to have the authority to operate bank accounts, execute government applications, and represent the Company in ordinary business within the scope of the specialty tea salon lounge business.

5. GOVERNANCE AND DEFERRED ACTIONS. The board adopts the internal administration manual, accepts the delegation of authority to the Representative Director in the ordinary course of business, and authorizes the filing of every business registration, food service report, civil defense fire clearance, tax registration, and environmental sewage certificate required for lawful operation.

6. EFFECTIVE DATE. This resolution shall be effective as of [Date], and the Company officers are authorized to certify copies and implement this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Financial Evidence Collection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized commercial bank handling domestic and foreign currency transactions in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary Korean Won account in the name of Yuhan Hoesa under pre-incorporation subscriber instructions. Each founding subscriber shall remit the subscribed capital contribution. The bank shall issue a certificate of paid-in capital deposit or passbook showing the full subscribed amount. The deposit must remain blocked until the company registration is completed and the tax office is notified. For non-resident subscribers, an exchange control declaration to the Foreign Exchange Bank is required when transferring funds from abroad. Prepare the capital contribution ledger showing subscriber identity, nationalities, passport numbers, amounts, and dates. After receiving the certificate, the authorized incorporator must retain it for submission with the company registration application.
required_dossiers: Certificate of paid-in capital deposit or original bank passbook showing full subscription amount
Subscriber identity and passport or government identification copies
Foreign exchange transaction record for each non-resident subscription
Share subscription application and contribution commitment schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds or requires a source of wealth explanation, provide a signed statement and supporting source documents. If the deposit is rejected, re-route the funds through another authorized bank and update the capital contribution ledger before resubmitting the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Registration of Articles of Incorporation with the District Court Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court, either through the Supreme Court eCourt portal or the court registration counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization or signature authentication of the Articles of Incorporation, file the company registration application with the competent District Court Registration Division. The application must include full incorporation facts, capital amount, registered office, and statutory officers. Submit the authenticated Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, registered office lease agreement or written consent of the building owner, appointment letters of officers, and identification evidence. The registration officer examines the filing for conformity with the Commercial Act. Once approved, the court records the company in the commercial register and issues a certificate of registered matters. The effective date of incorporation is the date of registration. The incorporators shall sign or seal the application and authorise the Representative Director to receive the certificate.
required_dossiers: Authenticated Articles of Incorporation
Application for company registration
Certificate of paid-in capital deposit
Registered office lease agreement or owner written consent
Letter of appointment and acceptance of statutory officers
Identification and employee number evidence of incorporators and officers
Power of attorney if filing through a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer issues a supplementary notice, cure the deficiency by filing the requested document within the statutory window. If the court suspects forged signatures, arrange personal appearance of the parties or obtain a new notarial authentication. If the registered office documentation is deficient, execute a corrected lease and file an amended application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Identification at the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, through the HomeTax portal or the competent local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After certified incorporation, apply for business registration with the competent tax office under the Corporate Tax Act and Value-Added Tax Act. Provide the corporate registration certificate, company seal certificate or digital certificate, registered office address, and anticipated business items matching the specialty tea salon lounge activities. Indicate that the corporate taxpayer will engage in food and beverage service and preparation at the registered premises. The tax office will assign a corporate registration number and a VAT business number. The company must also register its corporate digital certificate and mandatory e-tax invoice system. If the company has non-resident directors, appoint a domestic tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Keep the business registration certificate and tax identification numbers with the accounting records.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate
Business registration application form
Company seal certificate or digital certificate
Certificate of registered officers and Representative Director
Registered office lease agreement
Corporate bank account certificate
Subscriber and officer identification documents for tax purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service requests clarification of business scope, submit a revised business plan and ISIC code mapping. If the application is returned because the facility appears non-operational, provide the leasehold floor plan and food service licensing documents. Correct any postal or representative errors and re-file through HomeTax.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Service Business Report, Fire Safety Clearance, and Civil Defense Inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Si, Gun, or Gu municipal government and the fire inspectorate under the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety delegation and the National Fire Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a food service business report to the local health and sanitation division based on the Food Sanitation Act. Describe the premises as a specialty tea salon and general restaurant and provide the corporate certificate, lease contract, building floor plan, water and sewage connection documents, and kitchen equipment list. After the report is accepted, the sanitation authority may conduct a facility inspection. Concurrently, apply to the local fire station for a firefighting systems completion certificate and obtain a civil defense inspection under the fire prevention and installation maintenance laws. If the building is old or has a mezzanine, furnish a structural load inspection report. Provide allergen management and hygiene rules to the inspector. The final operating certificates are the Food Service Business Report Certificate and the Fire Safety Completion Certificate.
required_dossiers: Food service business report application form
Corporate registration certificate and business registration certificate
Lease agreement or proof of ownership of the tea salon premises
Building floor plan and total floor area calculation
Kitchen and sanitary facility equipment list
Water supply and sewage connection certificate
Fire safety facility design certificate and commissioning reports
Standard food hygiene management plan
Non-resident director identification and background certificate if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the food service report is queried for missing equipment, repair the facility and submit inspection photographs. If fire clearance is suspended, retain a licensed fire engineering consultant to upgrade sprinkler systems or evacuation signage and request a re-inspection. If the municipal government requires a building use change, file the building use change application before the final certificate is issued.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea - HomeTax online portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS for export declaration processing
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity commencing activity in Korea must, within 20 days of business commencement, file an Application for Business Registration (사업자등록 신청) with the competent district tax office that has jurisdiction over its Korean place of business or, in the absence of a Korean place of business, through a duly appointed tax representative. The application may be submitted online through HomeTax or physically at the district tax office. Required attachments include the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, foreign business registration certificate or equivalent foreign tax registration evidence, the entity's foreign tax identification number, proof of a Korean place of business (ownership deed or lease agreement), identity and authorization documents for the domestic tax representative, and apostilled or consular legalized constitutional documents. Upon acceptance, NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as both the corporate taxpayer identification number and the VAT registration number. A foreign corporation with no Korean business establishment and no VAT obligations may instead apply for a Foreigner Tax Code through the competent district tax office for purposes of domestic withholding and income tax compliance. A tax representative is mandatory for a foreign non-resident entity with Korean-source tax obligations and no fixed place of business in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Yuhan Hoesa is a statutory domestic corporation under the Korean Commercial Act and is taxed as a corporation under the Corporate Tax Act; no pass-through or transparent tax treatment is available)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korea does not operate a check-the-box or elective pass-through tax classification system. Available statutory elections include group tax consolidation for 100% owned Korean domestic subsidiaries, application for approval of a non-calendar business year, and simplified VAT taxpayer status for qualifying small businesses with annual revenue not exceeding KRW 80,000,000.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0; VAT registration is mandatory for every person carrying on an enterprise in Korea, with registration required within 20 days of business commencement. A simplified VAT taxpayer regime applies to small enterprises with annual revenue not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but this is a compliance simplification and does not exempt registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses issuing tax invoices must issue electronic tax invoices (전자세금계산서) through an NTS-compliant system and transmit them to HomeTax no later than the day following issuance. Electronic tax invoices must include the NTS-issued business registration numbers of both parties, supply date, taxable value, VAT, and a sequential electronic tax invoice number. Credit card sales data and cash receipt data are automatically transmitted to NTS for cross-matching. Korea does not use real-time fiscal digital stamping or continuous transaction control; instead NTS performs near-real-time validation and reconciliation through HomeTax. Licensed e-invoicing service providers must integrate with NTS HomeTax APIs and comply with the statutory electronic tax invoice serial-number standards.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to exported goods when a Korea Customs Service export declaration has been accepted and the goods physically leave Korea within the statutory period. Qualifying services supplied to non-residents, including offshore digital content services, are zero-rated when the recipient is a non-resident, the place of supply is outside Korea, and consideration is received in foreign currency or through foreign exchange settlement from the non-resident customer. For specialty tea and cultural ceramic goods sold to overseas consumers, each export shipment must be traceable to an accepted customs export declaration or an equivalent e-commerce export parcel record. The exporter must retain documentation evidencing actual shipment, export payment, and foreign exchange receipt in order to claim the corresponding input VAT credit or refund on the periodic VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration generated through UNI-PASS, referencing the Export Declaration Number and export value
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the goods, buyer, HS code, quantity, and total value
Main carriage document evidencing physical export: Bill of Lading for sea freight, Air Waybill for air freight, or postal/parcel dispatch certificate for e-commerce export
Foreign exchange receipt record issued by a Foreign Exchange Bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, proving repatriation of export proceeds in foreign currency
VAT export invoice or electronic tax invoice reflecting the 0% VAT rate and cross-referencing the export declaration number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS cross-checks zero-rated export claims against customs declarations, UNI-PASS records, Foreign Exchange Information System data, and bank remittance records. If the exporter fails to produce a valid customs export declaration and foreign exchange receipt evidence, NTS denies zero-rating, assesses the supply at the standard 10% VAT rate, and imposes additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including up to 40% of the understated tax for dishonest or fraudulent underreporting, plus overdue unpaid-tax additions. Intentional fabrication of export documentation or fraudulent VAT refund claims may trigger criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and the statutory assessment limitation period is extended to 10 years in cases of fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea, operating with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the central foreign exchange policy authority, and the Korea Customs Service as co-administrator of the Foreign Exchange Information System under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a fundamentally liberalized convertible currency regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is treated as a current-account convertible currency for trade, services, royalties, dividends, and loan interest, while capital-account transactions are open but subject to structured reporting rather than blanket pre-approval for standard foreign direct investment. Non-resident investors may own 100% of a Yuhan Hoesa and may remit dividends and disposed proceeds after corporate tax filings, tax clearance certificates, and external audit confirmation. However, treasury must manage several operational constraints: all foreign exchange transactions must route through an authorized foreign exchange bank; significant cross-border payments require documentary reasoning for settlement and settlement reporting under the Foreign Exchange Information System. There are no mandatory forced surrender conversion ratios for tea salon import payments, but export proceeds must be received within one year from the export declaration date. Account balances in Korean won cannot be transferred offshore without an underlying trade or investment; speculative won trading is prohibited, and the Bank of Korea and Korea Customs Service monitor volatility via macro-prudential limits, including FX liquidity guidance applied to banks. Profit remittance hurdles include the need to evidence corporate tax clearance, audited retained earnings, and compliance with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act registration if the entity enjoys foreign-investment protection.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exports of specialty tea, ceramics, or lounge-adjacent merchandise must be settled in foreign currency within one year of the export declaration date. Exporters may retain proceeds in an authorized foreign currency account or convert them to Korean won; no fixed statutory conversion ratio exists. If export proceeds are not collected by the one-year deadline, the exporter must obtain approval from the Korea Customs Service or the relevant foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and late settlement is subject to reporting penalties and potential loss of export incentive treatment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Korean Won Account
Multi-Currency Operating Account with Foreign Currency Deposit
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and Capital Verification Account
Foreign Direct Investment Escrow Account and Treasury Operating Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border fintech EMI viability is rated Very Low. In South Korea, only licensed foreign exchange banks authorized by the Financial Services Commission and the Bank of Korea may clear Korean won trade settlements, process foreign direct investment capital injection, and file Foreign Exchange Information System reports. Offshore digital EMIs cannot maintain a Korean won corporate settlement account, cannot provide local IBAN-equivalent clearing rails, and are not eligible to act as the receiving institution for paid-in capital verification. While certain domestic fintech licences exist under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act for money transfer business, these products must partner with a commercial bank for domestic settlement and cannot replace a tier-one treasury banking relationship. For KYC robustness, the entity should not use EMIs for capital injections or trade disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident directors, the statutory representative director must appear physically at the branch to establish personal identity and sign account agreements. Remote consular proxy opening is not uniformly accepted; most tier-one Korean banks require the physical appearance of the authorized signatory plus presentation of the original passport or alien registration card. A notarized and apostilled power of attorney may permit a third party to complete administrative formalities, but the bank reserves the right to conduct a video interview with the statutory director and call-back verification. In all cases, the foreign entity's corporate registration, articles of incorporation, UBO declaration, tax identification numbers, and underlying business documentation must be submitted for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The non-resident shareholder is an opaque shelf company in a secondary jurisdiction, preventing the Korean bank from identifying the natural-person controller and financial source of the paid-in capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The UBO must supply notarized corporate registry excerpts, apostilled certificate of good standing, an unbroken ownership chain diagram, a signed UBO declaration, personal tax identification numbers of all qualifying controllers, and six months of bank statements from the investing company showing the funds accumulating from verifiable operating income or declared shareholder loans.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The initial capital injection originates from a third-party wallet, virtual asset exchange, or an EMI which is not the registered foreign investing entity, triggering suspicion of layering or unverified source-of-funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The defense dossier must include a Swiss- or major-bank wire confirmation in the exact legal name of the foreign investor, a signed declaration of source of funds, audited financial statements or corporate tax returns for the investor, a dividend resolution if the funds are corporate profits, sales contracts for liquidated securities, and a foreign exchange bank traceability report showing the MT103 chain from the investor's segregated account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The specialty tea salon and lounge profile may be interpreted as a cash-intensive retail business, requiring transaction monitoring for potential cash structuring and under-declared revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The company must present the local business licence, food and beverage service licence, facility lease contract, detailed business plan including target average ticket price, POS system and settlement processor agreements, inventory purchase invoices, import customs declarations for tea and ceramics, a cash management policy limiting daily cash acceptance, and internal control procedures proving daily reconciliation of POS receipts to banking deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The foreign director's country of residence or the tea suppliers' source markets trigger sanctions, high-risk country, or PEP watchlist parameters despite the low-risk retail scope.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The company must submit evidence of beneficial owner and director sanctions/PEP negative screening from a reputable World-Check or Dow Jones supplier, import contracts with verified third-party suppliers, bill of lading and air waybill from the actual shipment journey, supplier commercial invoices, customs clearance certificates, and an explanatory memorandum proving that all personnel and counterparties are not located in comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be routed as a SWIFT MT103 or MT202 payment from the foreign shareholder's own account in a recognized banking jurisdiction directly to the Korean tier-one bank account maintained under the Yuhan Hoesa name. The Korean bank must file the foreign exchange settlement and investment reporting via the Foreign Exchange Information System using the capital transaction purpose code applicable to non-resident equity acquisition in a Korean limited liability company. After crediting the capital escrow account, a Korean certified public accountant or external auditor must issue a capital verification certificate confirming the paid-in capital and the share allotment. The entity must also register with the foreign direct investment system if statutory benefits are claimed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Funds from this escrow must remain frozen until the shareholder registry is updated and the tax authority declaration is filed, after which the company may transfer them into its general operating account for business use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of tea leaf imports, ceramic supplies, and merchant operating expenses, the company should use SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier payments, commercial letters of credit under ICC UCP600 for high-value new supplier transactions, and documentary collections on a D/P or D/A basis for established counterparties with clean trade history. Every outbound payment must be accompanied by a foreign exchange purpose code, commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, and optionally a conformity certificate if the payment is against a letter of credit. Inward trade collections and customer merchant receipts must be credited through the authorized foreign exchange bank and, when the currency differs from the operating currency, settled using the bank's transparent mid-market plus spread quotation with all transaction reports retained for tax and AML audit trails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won versus US dollar deliverable forward contracts with a demonstrable underlying trade receivable or payable matching face amount and tenor
Non-deliverable forwards on the Korean won with an authorized foreign exchange bank, limited to genuine export or import exposure and subject to documentary proof of the underlying trade
Cross-currency swaps permitted only for hedging actual foreign currency-denominated lease, loan, or supplier finance obligations, with no speculative leverage
Plain vanilla foreign exchange options with underlying committed trade flows and zero speculative rebalancing
Contractual netting for same-party recurring trade invoices through the corporate banking platform with explicit treasury policy approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax and Local Income Tax Surcharge)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax system, with local surcharge paid to the local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a December year-end, the due date is 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax under Article 47-2 of the Basic Law for National Taxes; daily interest of 0.012% of the overdue amount; persistent failure may trigger a tax enforcement investigation and administrative tax-levy seizure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax Return and Tax Invoice Filing for January-June period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 to 25 July of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional VAT of 10% of the tax amount assessed as non-payment penalty, plus daily overdue interest; revoked electronic tax invoice issuance status can trigger stricter supervision

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax Return and Tax Invoice Filing for July-December period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 to 25 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same as above: an additional 10% non-payment penalty and daily interest on overdue; continuous non-compliance can lead to forced closure of the tax domicile registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (AGM) and filing of the resolution if any amendments are required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Registry (court registry) for any amendments; no filing for the AGM itself
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year (generally convened by 30 June if fiscal year ends on 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No specific monetary fine for AGM non-observance, but failure to approve financial statements can invalidate dividend distributions; persistent non-observance can be sanctioned by court order upon shareholder petition

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Location Tax (per establishment) and local property-related annual levy payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Paid in October of each year (from 1 to 31 October); annual amount based on premises floor area
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 3% of unpaid local tax for late payment; after 30 days an additional 0.66% monthly penalty accrues; prolonged non-payment can result in coercive collection and seizure of business property

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory certified CPA audit is required for: (i) a company whose total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9 million); (ii) a company whose total revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.5 million) and whose average number of employees exceeds 100; (iii) small- and medium-sized enterprises with assets of KRW 7 billion or more if required by shareholders owning at least 3% of the equity; and (iv) any company publicly listed or regulated by the Financial Services Commission. The thresholds are based on the most recent fiscal year financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for publicly traded and large unlisted companies; Korean GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards) for smaller private companies, with the option of SME Accounting Standards for eligible small- and medium-sized enterprises

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently maintain a general public UBO register. However, every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and the transfer must be reported to the corporate registry when a change of controlling shareholder is disclosed for registration. Any transfer of shares or change of beneficial ownership must be reported to the National Tax Service through the shareholder ledger and, where the company is subject to the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, the relevant beneficial ownership declaration must be updated within 30 days from the event. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation form for ordinary private Ltd. companies.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per annum (only if triggered; typically USD 5,000 - USD 12,000 for a small specialty tea salon LLC under K-GAAP)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion, with progressive 10% (first KRW 200 million) and 20% (KRW 200 million to 20 billion) brackets, plus 10% local income tax surtax on the assessed national tax (effective top rate 24.2%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No free-zone or patent box regime applies to a specialty tea service; limited SME R&D tax credits and Foreign Investment Promotion Act incentives only for qualifying high-technology foreign investments; standard progressive rates apply

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Tax Base and Computed Tax Amount) filed electronically through HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) under Article 49 of the Framework Act on National Taxes
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending December 31, due by March 31 of the following year; for any other fiscal year-end, due within 3 months of the fiscal year-end; a non-resident corporation without a Korean permanent establishment is not required to file but is subject to final withholding at source

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and service revenue from the tea salon lounge, including in-store tea service, loose-leaf tea retail sales, ceramic art session fees, and online pre-paid voucher redemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate all Korean-source business receipts regardless of remittance; for a foreign corporation operating through a Korean permanent establishment, apply Article 8 of the Corporate Income Tax Act to apportion periodic business profits and reconcile declared amounts with VAT sales ledgers and POS Z-reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base after deducting net operating losses carried forward and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean branch of a foreign taxpayer, deduct qualifying NOLs that arose in the Korean business within the 10-year carryforward horizon; disallow any trade or business losses of the home office unless effectively connected with the Korean PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated corporate income tax by applying the statutory progressive rate schedule to the taxable income base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same brackets to a Korean PE as to a domestic company; foreign tax credits for foreign-source income taxed abroad may be claimed only through the Korean branch; no separate branch profits tax filing is made on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax obligations on outbound dividends, interest, and royalty payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the statutory 22% withholding on each category before applying any DTA-reduced rate; attach Form the Agreement for Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction, TRC, and beneficial ownership declaration; in the absence of documentation, withhold the full statutory amount and risk under-withholding penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Penalty surcharge assessed for late filing, non-payment, or underreporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, use this line to report any add-on penalties triggered by failure to file, and do not net criminal tax-evasion surcharges against treaty-exempt income; penalties remain collectible against Korean PE assets and responsible managers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net payable corporate income tax after deducting prepayments, interim taxes, and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure interim prepayment credits for the Korean branch are correctly allocated; if withholding credits arise from interest or royalty source income, reconcile them here; remit any residual balance by the extended due date or face daily surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% of the unpaid tax if filed after the due date, 20% if never filed, plus a 1.2% per month non-payment surcharge on tax paid late; understatement penalty of 10% for unsubstantiated claims; criminal tax evasion threshold: omission of KRW 50 million or 30% of tax due leading to imprisonment under the Punishment for Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax) on outbound dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders; DTA may reduce the rate to 5-15% depending on shareholding and treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the recipient must: (1) obtain an annual Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction; (2) execute a beneficial ownership declaration confirming active substance and no conduit arrangement; (3) submit the Application for Reduction/Exemption of Withholding Tax under Tax Treaty to the Korean payor before remittance; (4) allow the Korean paying company to produce this application when filing corporate tax; (5) if relief is denied, file a domestic wrongful-assessment appeal and, where applicable, a Mutual Agreement Procedure with the National Tax Service.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest is 22% each (20% national plus 2% local surtax); under most Korea-OECD DTAs, interest is capped at 10% (sometimes 5% for financial institutions) and royalties at 5-15%, with proportional reduction upon substantiation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File in Korea are required when international related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion in the preceding business year and total group revenue equals or exceeds KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report is due if consolidated turnover exceeds KRW 1 trillion; a specialty tea salon will nearly always be below these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not use UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the substance-over-form principle under the Framework Act on National Taxes and BEPS MLI Principal Purpose Test require the Korean tea salon and any foreign shareholder to perform genuine Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA)-local storefront, inventory, employees, and decision-making; lack of substance will deny treaty benefits and can recharacterize the Korean branch under the corporate veil-piercing doctrine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to record credit-card and POS-reconciled cash receipts from the tea salon lounge in the VAT and corporate income tax returns, repeated over consecutive fiscal years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 85(1) of the Punishment for Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine of up to 3 times the evaded tax; in flagrant cases exceeding KRW 50 million in omitted tax, the Director must file a criminal complaint with the Public Prosecutor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for evaded tax plus 20% wrongful-reduction surcharge; a travel ban is issued against the responsible director, the corporate veil is pierced to attach personal bank accounts, and criminal imprisonment of 1-3 years may be imposed if the board knowingly approved suppressed revenue schedules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated brand use royalties or management fees to an overseas shareholder/affiliate for a tea-brand name that holds no trademark, employee, or actual marketing activity in Korea, and omitting contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 9 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, the National Tax Service re-determines the arm's length amount, adds 10% TP adjustment penalty, and imposes neglect/understatement surcharges of up to 20% of the underpaid corporate tax; the unilateral relief cannot be used as a defense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute the phantom service agreement are jointly and severally liable under the commercial manager's duty for unjustified corporate outflow; assets may be attributed to the director personally, the director may be blacklisted from exiting Korea, and criminal liability under Article 85 of the Punishment for Tax Evaders Act applies if the false fee was knowingly used to shift profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Treaty Abuse (False DTA Withholding Claim)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A nominee foreign shareholder with no office, staff, or dividend-course activity in its residence jurisdiction uses a bilateral treaty to withhold dividend remittances at 5% instead of the statutory 22%, submitting a forged Tax Residency Certificate and a bare beneficial ownership declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 5-2 of the International Tax Adjustment Act denies treaty benefits retroactively; the Korean company is assessed the 20% difference plus 10% underreporting penalty and monthly overdue interest; the tax treaty's Mutual Agreement Procedure is inapplicable to the sham entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean directors who allowed the false declaration are subject to piercing of the corporate veil under the company behind the company principle, personal civil liability for the denied withholding tax plus penalties, a Korean travel ban (blacklisting) during investigation, and up to 3 years of imprisonment for aiding false official documents.
